dependency.note: Dependent Grade5proposal including prior reviewed components; not accepted-main or deployment status.

interpretation: Semantic authoring judgments do not certify learner mastery, delivered performance or consumer eligibility. Whole/component, prerequisite and candidate-only support are distinguished. Conditions do not authorize new topics or changes to claims. Later full claims are not lowered from a matching component; existing possible duplicates remain unchanged.

supportingResources.title: Emerald ash borer
supportingResources.role: Verify Ontario presence and native-ash feeding/mortality case; supplementary localization, not curriculum authority or pest-management advice.

expectations.rationale: Existing investigation/design/data/risk operations contribute; integrated scientific performance, appropriate resources and audience fit remain.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Question selection, close observation, shared fact gathering and evidence-based reporting have existing claims.
remainingConditions: Check an integrated research performance in the science strands; the collection of generic claims is not a completed investigation. Process guidance is flexible by readiness, not a requirement for advanced bibliography or bias analysis in Grade 6.

expectations.rationale: Existing claims cover guided experiments, predictions, recording and conclusions without importing later formal hypothesis/variable terminology. Existing independently planned variables, repeat-measurement and data-evidence claims also contribute; these are available operations, not a mandatory advanced checklist. The age-fit hypothesis/investigation claim contributes variable/sample/risk planning, without inventing a mandatory Ontario template.
remainingConditions: A safe, connected performance in relevant science content remains to be demonstrated.

expectations.rationale: Sketches, safe making, motion-design testing and comparisons supply existing engineering operations appropriate to the Grade 6 body content. Existing prototype testing explicitly controls variables and diagnoses failures.
remainingConditions: Assess a coherent design/build/test performance, its evidence and response to results; isolated operations are insufficient.
Use readiness-dependent process guidance without requiring every advanced engineering step.

expectations.rationale: The safety and early making claims include hazard-aware plans, safe sensory exploration, careful equipment use and cleanup. The existing risk-plan evidence explicitly selects protective equipment and records controls, with actual safe performance still to check.
remainingConditions: Explicitly check task-appropriate protective clothing/equipment in addition to general safe handling. Later drilling-specific safeguards do not supply a universal early investigation claim.

expectations.rationale: Scientific reporting and existing vocabulary/audience decisions are reusable. Existing causal conclusions/confidence reporting and complex data representation supply further communication operations; audience fit remains to assess.
remainingConditions: Check the actual scientific vocabulary and audience/format choices in a science report; generic vocabulary or writing-process success alone does not certify the integrated requirement.

expectations.rationale: Varied input and coding operations are present; applied science purposes and complete impact cases remain.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Existing input/branching evidence uses key presses, typed answers and sensing conditions; computer-component selection identifies input devices and their purposes.
remainingConditions: Use varied inputs in written/executed scientific investigations/models and explain the purpose. Naming a microphone is not equivalent to programming its input.

expectations.rationale: Everyday AI examples include benefits and limitations, providing a direct emerging-technology contribution. The existing digital-impact claim assesses community benefit/exclusion, wellbeing and environmental effects; science/trades applications remain explicit.
remainingConditions: Explain an effect of programmed behaviour as well as an emerging-technology example; device naming alone is insufficient.

deferredCandidates.reason: Broader historical effects can support discussion, but do not themselves explain the role of a programmed instruction.

expectations.rationale: Practical applications have support; interdisciplinary performance and verified contribution cases remain.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Purposeful products and places, together with property-to-function explanations, support familiar scientific/design applications. Use a relevant example such as a spill-resistant container and its material choice, not an unrelated device list.
Motion-design testing supplies science/data work and shared research supplies information gathering and writing.
remainingConditions: Assess the integrated use of another subject in a real problem; co-listing generic skills is insufficient.

expectations.rationale: Existing biography, community-history and ecological-knowledge claims provide candidates; the resource task does not justify separate community clones.
remainingConditions: Verify age-appropriate resources from multiple communities and examine what the contributions changed.
Do not treat a single biography or a generic ecological statement as complete evidence.

deferredCandidates.reason: One scientific biography is a possible example, not a multi-community review.
Requires factual/cultural and whole-claim review before contextual reuse.
Investigating the importance of a local person or group can support the process, but scientific contributions and multiple communities need verified content.

expectations.rationale: Benefits/loss explanations contribute; the local planned-and-enacted response remains explicit.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: The existing biodiversity claim explicitly explains stability, resilience and ecosystem services and predicts a cascade from changing a key species. Assess benefits and consequences using a suitable checked case rather than only counting species.
Existing sourced conservation cases, considered perspectives and ordered task planning provide substantive components.
remainingConditions: Analyse a checked local issue, plan a justified response and actually carry it out. A proposed action or description of another community is not evidence that the learner acted.

expectations.rationale: Classification, variation, threats and ecological relationships contribute; complete multi-level/community integration and cultural-agriculture cases remain.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Existing broad organism classification, evidence-based unfamiliar-organism reasoning and branching keys supply a system and more detailed grouping. A compulsory advanced taxonomic-rank list is not invented.

contributions.topicName: Plants and animals in their habitats

expectations.rationale: Species variety, measured within-species trait variation and contrasting organism/habitat models are real existing contributions.
remainingConditions: Make the complete within-species, community and habitat-level diversity account explicit. A species-count definition alone does not establish every level.

deferredCandidates.reason: The complete later claim defines genetic/species/ecosystem levels and threats; no11–12context is inferred from one overlapping clause.

expectations.rationale: The existing complete claim explicitly links variation among same-species individuals to environmental advantage, survival and reproduction. Use a changed-condition case that explains why variation matters for the group rather than treating every trait difference as beneficial.
The current biodiversity evidence explicitly explains stability/resilience and cascades, so community resilience is not treated as absent.
remainingConditions: Explain the complete within-and-among-community resilience relationship using appropriate cases. A single keystone-removal story alone does not establish all scales.

deferredCandidates.reason: The full later multi-level biodiversity/threat claim remains unchanged; it is not lowered solely because resilience appears here.

expectations.rationale: Colony cooperation, between-species symbiosis, food-web interdependence and organism-driven habitat change cover actual categories of interaction.
remainingConditions: Integrate those relationships with an explained biodiversity-sustaining outcome. Naming social roles or food-web arrows alone does not prove the complete account.

expectations.rationale: The existing invasive-species claim explains introduction and harms to native organisms, while biodiversity explains ecological consequences. The checked CFIA example confirms emerald ash borer in Ontario and its native-ash damage mechanism; assess the justified local effect rather than a new country-specific topic.
remainingConditions: Distinguish a harmful introduction from harmless non-native status, and population decline from automatic proof of immediate species extinction.

expectations.rationale: Existing climate warming, environmental-change threats to survival and biodiversity cascades together supply the causal chain and consequences. Later detailed range-shift or molecular greenhouse accounts are not required for this selected explanation.
Existing pollinator/food-security explanations and food-production systems supply real agricultural biodiversity components.
remainingConditions: Use checked Indigenous agricultural cases and explain how diversity supports them. Generic farming or an unsourced cultural label does not establish the required worldwide account.

deferredCandidates.reason: Existing rainforest ecological-use knowledge includes farming, but requires factual/cultural source review and does not stand in for the full worldwide case set.

expectations.rationale: Resource and climate effects contribute; Canadian/community-specific impact judgments and actual advocacy remain.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Resource extraction/use effects, fossil-fuel warming and community energy/conservation cases contribute directly.
remainingConditions: Assess verified Canadian generation cases over relevant timescales, including the named communities and climate/social effects. Generic energy-source labels do not establish local or community-specific impacts.

expectations.rationale: Existing technology energy-use assessment, source classification and community action explanations supply components.
remainingConditions: Justify actual electricity-reducing choices across sources and carry out school-community advocacy. A private intention or a conservation slogan alone is not that performance.

expectations.rationale: Static/current, materials, output conversions and components have support; varied generation and circuit-use cases remain.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: The existing full claim explains frictional electron transfer, attraction/repulsion and everyday discharge. It already supports observed electrostatic cases at its current complete age fit.

contributions.topicName: Current, voltage, and what they measure

expectations.rationale: Current-as-charge-flow and static charge accumulation/discharge have explicit existing explanations. Assess the comparison directly, rather than treating every electrical event as the same type.
The existing claim tests and classifies multiple materials and explains metal wiring with insulating coatings. No older conductor-list topic is required.
The existing conservation-case evidence explicitly explains solar panels converting sunlight to electricity; device-design evidence explains an authored energy conversion.
remainingConditions: Check varied generation inputs and the actual conversion to electrical output. Building a solar oven or naming a renewable source does not establish an electrical generator.

expectations.rationale: Existing everyday transformations, device conversions and source-to-destination light/sound/heat examples support varied electrical-output cases. Assess the actual conversion path rather than only appliance names.
The existing complete circuit-building claim explicitly names cells, wires, bulbs, switches and buzzers and explains their roles. No component-purpose clone is added.
The existing vocabulary evidence explicitly distinguishes the configurations and their electrical differences.
remainingConditions: Assess suitable everyday uses and the reason for each configuration. Distinguishing two diagrams alone is not the complete applications account.

deferredCandidates.reason: The complete later current/voltage/resistance rule and practical-use claim begins at12; no11–12context is inferred solely from a simpler distinction.

expectations.rationale: Overall environmental aviation impacts are not inferred from the single societal child requirement. Verified environmental cases remain to review.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Design trade-offs and transport/energy knowledge exist, but no complete checked aviation-impact case is established. The overall environmental judgment is reviewed separately from this societal specific requirement.
remainingConditions: Evaluate actual local/global societal effects and perspectives using appropriate sources. An aircraft name, generic carbon word or unrelated travel story is insufficient.

deferredCandidates.reason: Generic cost/safety/function/sustainability trade-offs may support a verified aviation task, but do not establish its factual impacts.

expectations.rationale: Existing drag, weight, balance and structure/function components are real; complete four-force flight/control accounts retain conditions.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Existing parachute/drag explanations and air-pressure/weight knowledge are real relevant components.
remainingConditions: Relate selected properties to actual flight applications, rather than equating atmospheric pressure or gas space filling with a complete lift explanation.

expectations.rationale: Drag depends on movement/area, weight is gravitational force and force diagrams compare magnitudes/directions. These are substantive components of the selected relationship.
remainingConditions: Explain all four flight forces and their relationships in a checked flight case. Upthrust vocabulary is not automatically an assessed aerodynamic lift claim, and two-force balance is not the complete four-force account.

expectations.rationale: Existing claims predict motion from balance and represent multiple forces, contributing the general physical account.
remainingConditions: Show actual flight-control cases in machines and organisms. A stationary-book diagram does not itself establish those applications.

expectations.rationale: Existing speed/area effects on drag and mass/gravity effects on weight provide actual adjustable components.
remainingConditions: Explain appropriate lift/thrust changes and relate all selected force changes to flight. A generic force-strength word does not establish each control method.

expectations.rationale: Existing structure-function arguments include bird wings, and body-group comparison distinguishes physical features. These contribute actual characteristics rather than a topic-title match.
remainingConditions: Explain how varied organism characteristics enable flight. Naming wings or an evolutionary ancestor alone does not complete the function account.

deferredCandidates.reason: The existing full fossil/flight-origin evidence claim is a distinct operation and is not automatically a holder for present-day flight function.
The body-plan claim includes insect wing presence but its main evidence is anatomy/grouping; it does not certify a complete flight-function account.

expectations.rationale: Earth-observation components contribute; verified space-needs and impact judgments remain.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: General human needs and coping knowledge exist, but the actual space-condition and response account is not established by a basic astronaut/ISS label.
remainingConditions: Use verified space-condition and supported needs/response cases. Do not substitute a general food/water list for actual space accommodation.

deferredCandidates.reason: The complete later Mars/SETI claim includes radiation, low-gravity and isolation but begins at13 and has substantial additional demands; it is not lowered for one matching space-needs clause.
General human needs are useful content but do not themselves demonstrate how needs are met in space.
General coping evaluation does not establish actual space psychological conditions or practices.

expectations.rationale: Existing weather satellites and modern polar-science technologies provide real Earth-observation/climate components.
remainingConditions: Assess the observational role using checked environmental-change/climate evidence. A weather forecast or a satellite name alone is not a long-term change assessment.

expectations.rationale: Current exploration-history and general design-trade-off knowledge are relevant, but are not treated as verified impact judgments.
remainingConditions: Evaluate actual effects with appropriate evidence and perspectives; programme dates and names alone are insufficient.

deferredCandidates.reason: Exploration history provides context but its evidence does not assess the full social/environment impact account.
General sustainability/cost/safety trade-offs require verified space cases before they establish these effects.

expectations.rationale: The selected object, gravity, light, geometry and technology specifics have support; broad integrated understanding is not certified by a union of links.
remainingConditions: No overall judgment is certified by child-link totals or a differently scoped child requirement.

expectations.rationale: Existing detailed planet distinctions, small-body composition, spherical Sun/Earth/Moon models and Sun light/heat descriptions supply the complete selected object set and physical contrasts. No separate Ontario solar-system list is introduced.

The existing complete claim distinguishes matter amount from gravitational force with units and changing gravitational-field examples. Its complete age fit already begins at11; no earlier lowering is needed.
The existing claim explicitly relates weight to mass and gravitational field strength and predicts other-world changes. The same stable knowledge supports the source relationship.

The existing star claim identifies the Sun as a star and the sky-object claim explicitly states its light output; the Moon claim contrasts reflected sunlight with own-light production. Use those actual body-type distinctions, not the false rule that every bright object emits its own light.
Existing rotation/year, phases/eclipses and tilt/polar-season explanations supply several distinct effects of relative geometry and movement. No unrelated orbital-mechanics equations are imposed.
Existing telescope observations, robotic data collection and changed-model evidence explicitly connect technologies with what scientists can learn. This is more than a history list of launch dates.
